rationale: The workflow already implements the applicable dependency-caching optimization via `astral-sh/setup-uv@v7` with `enable-cache: true` and `cache-dependency-glob: "pyproject.toml"`, which caches uv dependency downloads. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE / P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE evidence (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) measured ~9.2% savings from adding `actions/cache@v4` for `~/.cache/pip` keyed by `pyproject.toml`, but its contraindication "An equivalent cache already exists" applies here because uv's built-in cache already performs the same dependency download caching. Adding a separate pip cache would be redundant and is not compatible with uv's cache layout. Stale-run cancellation (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) is already present via `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` for non-protected refs. No matrix exists for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT lacks representative successful-duration history (only two runs with widely varying durations) and risks failing valid slow runs, so no safe timeout value can be proposed from available evidence.
